finding: An inline double-quoted git commit -m message executed backtick command substitutions before git received the message; one substitution ran node bin/backtest.mjs from repo root and recorded empty spans.

ruling.why: Shared main cannot be amended or rewritten safely. A git note preserves the original commit and records the damage without changing history.
ruling.required_rule: Use git commit -F <message-file> only in this shared worktree. The message file is written as data, reviewed, and passed without shell interpolation.

stronger_boundary.why_hooks_cannot_fully_prevent: Command substitution occurs in the invoking shell before git or a git hook runs; a commit-msg hook cannot undo code execution that already happened.
stronger_boundary.recommended_control: Use an allowlisted commit wrapper or command policy that requires -F and refuses inline -m in the shared worktree; keep the tick rule as the human/agent contract.
stronger_boundary.no_secret_claim: Do not place secrets in commit messages; shell execution risk is broader than secret leakage.

history_audit.observed: Historical commit messages contain backticks and shell-looking prose, but stored git messages do not record whether the original invocation used -m or -F, nor whether a substitution executed.
history_audit.03059df: Confirmed incident and noted via git notes.
history_audit.earlier_messages: No additional execution can be proven from the git object history alone. Do not claim a clean retrospective scan; inspect shell/agent command logs if a complete incident census is required.

no_claim: No claim that git notes prevent recurrence, no claim that earlier backticks were executed, and no claim that a commit hook can intercept shell substitution.
